extracted.intended_audience: registered apprenticeship program sponsors, participating employers, Registration Agencies, and apprenticeship system stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts regulatory requirements and evaluative criteria from a Department of Labor proposed rule (29 CFR part 29) governing registration, program agreements, trainer/provider qualifications, and National Occupational Standards for registered apprenticeship programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-part review for programs with 1–2 year training cycles
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(d)(1) describes two scenarios after a Registration Agency approves an application: if a provisionally registered program has completed its first full training cycle, it would be granted permanent registration; if it has not completed its first training cycle, it would remain provisionally approved until its subsequent program review at the end of the first full training cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed for programs with full training cycles longer than 1 year but ≤2 years to allow programmatic efficiencies and to coincide with the requirement in 29 CFR 30.4(e) for an initial written affirmative action plan within 2 years of registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deregistration procedures for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(d)(2) provides that if a program is not found to be operating in compliance with this part and part 30, it would be subject to the deregistration procedures at proposed §29.20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration Agencies may provide technical assistance and enhanced oversight (per proposed §29.20(a)) so programs found noncompliant may receive assistance prior to formal deregistration actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent program reviews for permanently registered programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(d)(3) provides that programs receiving permanent registration would be subject to subsequent program reviews by Registration Agencies as provided in proposed §29.19.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permanent registration does not remove ongoing review obligations; such programs remain subject to periodic oversight per §29.19.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum apprentice enrollment requirement (at least one apprentice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(e) incorporates the existing requirement that every registered apprenticeship program must have at least one apprentice and adds that failure to comply could result in deregistration proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirement includes two allowable gap periods (each not to exceed 1 year): (1) between program registration and registration of first apprentice(s); (2) between graduation of an apprentice and registration of the next apprentice(s). Intended as administrative safeguard against programs that register but never enroll apprentices; Department solicits comments on longer latency periods for special circumstances (e.g., economic downturns). Programs deregistered for zero apprentices may reregister if they meet requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprentice completion rate metrics (annual and cohort)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department is proposing two different completion rate metrics (annual and cohort) to assess program completion performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metrics aim to ensure programs seek to graduate apprentices rather than merely access federal benefits; the Department requests comments on scenarios where apprentices are enrolled but not successfully graduated or converted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process and timelines for modifications to standards of apprenticeship
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(f) requires sponsors to submit any proposals for modifications or changes to standards of apprenticeship or certified National Guidelines to the Registration Agency, which must determine consistency with this part and 29 CFR part 30 and, if consistent, approve within 90 calendar days from receipt of a complete submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If approved, modifications must be recorded and acknowledged within 90 calendar days of approval; if not approved, sponsors must be notified of the disapproval reasons and provided appropriate technical assistance. Clarifies review, approval, recording, and technical assistance timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory terms of program standards adoption agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.11(a) would require that program standards adoption agreements (between a sponsor and a participating employer reached outside collective bargaining) include that the participating employer will: (1) adopt and comply with the sponsor's registered standards of apprenticeship; (2) comply with all other applicable requirements in this part; and (3) cooperate with and provide assistance to the sponsor, including providing apprenticeship-related data and records necessary to assess compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to ensure participating employers' accountability for compliance and to hold sponsors accountable for entities they partner with; modeled after existing Employer Acceptance Agreement (Appendix D of OA boilerplate standards). Sponsors must clearly articulate these obligations in every adoption agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: 30-day transmission requirement for adoption agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.11(b) requires transmission of the program standards adoption agreement to the Registration Agency within 30 days of execution of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows the Registration Agency to verify compliance and engage in oversight; helps ensure employers understand obligations as employers of apprentices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participating employer cancellation right (30-day notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.11(c)(1) provides that a participating employer may cancel the program standards adoption agreement by providing 30 days written notice to the sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department anticipates employers cancelling when they have no apprentices employed (e.g., apprentices converted to regular employees, ended OJT, or placed with a different employer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor suspension/cancellation duty for noncompliant participating employers
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.11(c)(2) provides that a sponsor must suspend or cancel the adoption agreement if it determines the participating employer failed to satisfy the mandatory terms in §29.11(a); the sponsor is responsible for determining compliance and taking action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsor must monitor participating employers; failure to suspend or cancel as required may lead Registration Agency to initiate deregistration proceedings under §29.20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirements for suspension or cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.11(c)(2)(i) requires the program sponsor to provide written notice of any suspension or cancellation to the participating employer, all affected apprentices, and the applicable Registration Agency, explaining the reason for the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures adequate written notice to everyone affected and transparency about reasons for suspension/cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprentice placement obligation upon interruption/cessation of training
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.11(c)(2)(ii) requires that if suspension or cancellation results in interruption or cessation of training, the sponsor must make a reasonable effort to place affected apprentices with another of the sponsor's participating employers or a different registered apprenticeship program in the same occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to protect apprentices' training continuity; Registration Agencies may provide technical assistance upon request if the sponsor encounters placement challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration Agency enforcement for sponsor neglect regarding adoption agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.11(c)(2)(iii) provides that if a program sponsor fails to suspend or cancel an adoption agreement as required, the Registration Agency could initiate deregistration proceedings against the sponsor pursuant to proposed §29.20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals the importance of sponsor monitoring of participating employers and the risk of deregistration for neglecting these obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainer mastery of occupation-specific skills, techniques, and competencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.12(a)(1) states that apprentice trainers or providers of related instruction must possess a mastery of the relevant job skills, techniques, and relevant competencies of the occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mastery is required so trainers can impart proficiency to apprentices; critical for apprentices to become proficient in critical job tasks, particularly in time-sensitive occupations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainer continuous learning and upskilling obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.12(a)(2) requires journeyworkers to stay up to date on advances in technology, technical knowledge, new and emerging techniques, and evolving job skills necessary to maintain proficiency and mastery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures apprentices learn contemporary, relevant skills amid technological and workplace changes (digital tools, remote work); supports continuous learning/upskilling for trainers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainer communication and demonstration capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.12(a)(3) requires that journeyworkers be effective communicators capable of transmitting and demonstrating specialized knowledge, job skills, techniques, or processes required to achieve occupational proficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communication skill is essential so trainers can pass their mastery to apprentices through effective demonstration and explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainer evaluation and competency assessment skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.12(a)(4) requires trainers to evaluate apprentices' progress and performance fairly and objectively throughout a program, including assessing attainment of competencies during on-the-job training and recognizing when apprentices are proficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes fair, transparent, and equitable evaluation (DEIA lens); apprentices advance by attainment of competencies over a minimum duration of on-the-job time; acceleration is allowed only when an apprentice is demonstrably proficient, not merely to expedite completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainer linkage of related instruction to on-the-job tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.12(a)(5) requires trainers to establish practical connections between conceptual/theoretical knowledge from related instruction and its implications/applications for the occupation (why instruction matters and how to perform tasks successfully).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps apprentices understand the relevance of related instruction and improves transfer of classroom learning to practical job performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainer obligations for safe, inclusive, and EEO-compliant environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.12(b) requires journeyworkers to help ensure apprentices receive training in a safe and inclusive work environment; trainers must have completed anti-harassment trainings required in part 30 and should not have a record of substantiated noncompliance with EEO requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounded in DEIA research and OA guidance: inclusive leaders and mentors support diverse apprentices, improve retention and recruitment; DEIA training encouraged as a best practice though not required; technical and policy rationale provided for embedding inclusive practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related instruction provider qualifications (faculty/state-certified/SME)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.12(c)(1) would require providers of related instruction to be faculty/instructors at an accredited postsecondary institution or meet the State's certification requirements for CTE instructors; a subject-matter expert (e.g., a journeyworker) may also provide related instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies existing regulatory text, preserves flexibility for journeyworkers to provide instruction, and ensures instructors are capable educators capable of communicating complex subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related instruction teaching techniques and adult learning competency
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.12(c)(2) retains the existing requirement that instructors possess skills in teaching techniques for different audiences, including adult learning styles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses diverse apprentice backgrounds (many are adult learners); instructors must understand adult-learning principles and apply appropriate techniques to ensure comprehension across audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical assistance and trainer development support commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department commits to providing technical assistance to help programs comply with trainer and instructor qualification requirements and to promote mentorships, templates for trainer/instructor assessment, and a system-wide network (contemplated 'Registered Apprenticeship Academy') to facilitate mentoring and trainer development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to streamline compliance, create feedback loops, and support trainer development and program success; not a regulatory requirement but an implementation support mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and criteria for National Occupational Standards for Apprenticeship
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.13 describes development and intended use of industry-validated National Occupational Standards for Apprenticeship: national, off-the-shelf resources to accelerate development of registered apprenticeship programs in occupations of national scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OA will convene industry stakeholders to develop standards; Administrator will review and approve standards using criteria including suitability under §29.7, an industry-validated work process schedule, a nationally applicable, industry-validated curriculum framework for related instruction, methods for ongoing evaluation of apprentices, interim credentials, and industry-validated end-point assessments. Standards are intended to drive system quality and, as developed, would be required for national-scope programs per proposed §§29.14 and 29.15. The process is proactive and industry-vetted (not first-come-first-served); public comment will be sought.
